content.title: Charlie May - Men's Basketball - University of Michigan Athletics
content.text: Who is Charlie May? • Tireless worker; valuable teammate • Relentless and tireless defender • Excellent in transition; strong court vision • Not afraid to battle for rebounds • Ability to score inside and from long range • Son of head coach Dusty May; strong basketball IQ Career: Michigan • Helped Michigan to an outright Big Ten regular-season title (2025-26) • U-M’s first regular-season title since 2020-21 • Led Michigan to a program and Big Ten-best 19-1 conference record • Helped Michigan to the Big Ten Tournament title (2025) • U-M's fourth conference tournament championship • Earned automatic bid to NCAA Tournament • Helped Michigan to NCAA Tournament (2025) • Awarded No. 5-seed in South Regional • Defeated No. 12-seed UC San Diego (68-65) in first round • Defeated No. 4-seed Texas A&M (91-79) in second round • In Sweet 16, lost to No. 1-seed Auburn (78-65) • Helped U-M to NCAA Tournament (2026) • Awarded No. 3 overall seed, No. 1-seed in Midwest Regional • No. 1 seed for the fourth time in program history (1985, 1993, 2021, 2026) Season: 2025-26 (Michigan) • Played in six games off the bench • Scored first career points on a three-pointer against Oakland (Nov. 3) Season: 2024-25 (Michigan) • Played in five games: all off the bench • Grabbed a rebound (2x): Cleveland State (Nov. 4) and Miami (Ohio) (Nov. 18) Season: 2023-24 (Central Florida) • Played in six games: all off the bench • Made collegiate debut against Florida International (Nov. 6); played in the final minute • Grabbed a rebound (3x): Lipscomb (Dec. 2), Jacksonville (Dec. 6), and Maine (Dec. 18) • Had first career steal against Bethune-Cookman (Dec. 29) Season: 2022-23 (Central Florida) • Walk-on; redshirted the season • Valuable scout team/practice squad member Career: Prep • Prepped at Saint Andrew's School under Coach John O'Connell • Compiled an 80-21 record in four seasons • Member of the 2020 Class 3A State Championship team • (3x) District 12 champions • Team Captain (2021-22) • As a senior (2021-22), averaged 7.4 points, 7.0 rebounds, and 3.4 assists; helped Scots to an 18-8 record and advance to the Class 3A regional quarterfinal, falling to Santa Fe Catholic (66-55); recorded six double-figure scoring games with a season-best 19 points against King's Academy (Jan. 25); recorded six double-figure rebounding games with a season-best 14 against the Everglades (Nov. 27); had three double-doubles and 10 games with five-plus assists with a season-best seven Berean Christian (Dec. 2); had a career-best six steals (2x): Ransom Everglades (Jan. 7) and Pine Crest (Jan. 28) • As a junior (2020-21), averaged 2.6 points and 1.4 rebounds; helped Scots to an 11-6 record, the District 11 title, and advance to the Class 3A regional semifinal, falling to Calvary Christian Academy (61-58); scored a season-best 12 points against Elite Academy (Jan. 8); had a season-best four rebounds (2x) and three assists against Oxbridge Academy (Jan. 12) • As a sophomore (2019-20), helped Scots to a 26-5 record, the District 11 title and win the Class 3A State championship defeating Andrew Jackson (57-50); advanced to the Class 3A Final Four after winning the Region 3 title over Santa Fe Catholic (83-62); defeated Westminster (70-61) and Sagemont (62-51) in the semifinal and quarterfinals, respectively • As a freshman (2018-19), helped Scots to a 25-5 record, the District 12 title, and advanced to the Class 5A Region 3 championship, falling to Tampa Catholic (62-59) Notables • Son of Michigan head coach Dusty May • Older brother, Jack, was a guard with Florida and completed his redshirt junior campaign in the 2023-24 season • Won 2020 Florida Class 3A state title with brother, Jack, at Saint Andrew's School
